correctness.rationale: For any independent dominating set D, the selected original vertices S form a clique in G, hence |S|<=2 because G is triangle-free. Each subdivision vertex is either excluded by independence if incident to S, or forced by domination otherwise. An unselected original vertex is undominated precisely when its full original neighborhood equals S. For S=empty connectedness excludes this; for a singleton it is exactly a leaf neighbor obstruction; for an edge it would force a triangle and is impossible. This proves a nonoverlapping bijection with the three templates. Direct degree counting gives the bivariate formula. The minimum coefficient formula follows by comparing each exponent to the maximal edge-degree-sum bound; all 88 connected triangle-free unlabeled atlas graphs through order seven, 3,098,568 subsets, match the bivariate theorem and count.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary source states a scalar minimum formula for central graphs and, in its proof, uses original cliques and forced subdivision choices for selected minimum sets. It does not give an all-independent-dominating-set bijection, any independent domination polynomial of central graphs, a linear exact count for all maximal independent sets, or edge-degree-sum coefficient recovery. The independently inspected 2014 polynomial paper gives the notion and formulas for original standard graph classes, not their central graph transform. Closest published-finding corpus central-graph findings concern higher-iterate scalar independent domination or first-iterate total domination. The claimed novelty is therefore the complete bivariate census and its structural consequences, not the already known scalar minimum. Search is evidence of noncoverage, not global uniqueness.
residual_risks: Original paper Theorem 2.1 includes closely related clique/forced-subdivision ideas; an equivalent all-set identity could be regarded as implicit in its argument even though no enumeration theorem is stated.
Older work on maximal independent sets in central graphs could use different terminology or lack indexing; searches do not prove global uniqueness.
The bivariate variable distinguishes original vertices, so order-three cases require the construction marking explicitly.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural all-solutions question immediately motivated by a new scalar independent-domination result. Unlike a routine recalculation of the minimum, it proves that all maximal independent sets of central graphs of an arbitrary connected triangle-free original can be completely enumerated in linear output size, not exponentially, gives their entire bivariate size distribution, and extracts original edge degree-sum frequencies. The two six-vertex spiders show the polynomial reveals structural information invisible to the original degree sequence. The result applies to an infinite broad class, has an explicit algorithm and precise optimal-solution multiplicities.
